requirement:
Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas-refactor` skill whose description tells agents to
use it when a change moves code, tests, or requirements to another file,
chapter, or outline node, including splitting or merging modules or chapters,
or renames a requirement, so that evidence whose content is unchanged is not
invalidated.
rationale:
structural: The only structural obligation in `requirements.cli.refactor_skill` is that Habeas bundles a skill named `habeas-refactor` whose description tells agents when to use it. The skill file is the artifact, and the review root `assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md` is that file. Its front matter has `name: habeas-refactor`. Its `description` begins "Use when a change moves code, tests, or requirements ... to another file, chapter, or outline node". It then covers splitting or merging modules or chapters and moving or renaming a requirement. It ends with the stated purpose, "so that evidence whose content is unchanged is not invalidated". Every clause of the requirement is therefore met by the root. Bundling the skill is carried by the `assets/skills` directory, which `Cargo.toml` already lists as the skills source (`table[package.metadata.symposium.skills]`). The requirement names no library, algorithm, type or signature, so how the directory is shipped is not a structural obligation. No other root needs an `{impl}` reference. The text is about what the skill file says, so nothing else is left to cover.

behavioral: The subject has one observable obligation: the bundled `habeas-refactor` skill's description must tell agents to use it when a change moves code, tests, or requirements to another file, chapter, or outline node. This includes splitting or merging modules or chapters, and renaming a requirement. The stated purpose is that evidence whose content is unchanged is not invalidated.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_refactor_skill_is_used_for_moves_and_requirement_renames]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It reads the front-matter description of `habeas-refactor` through the helpers `description`, `skill_md` and `skill_files`. `skill_files` embeds `assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md` with `include_str!`. It asserts that the description contains four phrases:
- "Use when a change moves code, tests, or requirements in a Habeas project to another file, chapter, or outline node" covers the use-when trigger and the three kinds of target.
- "splitting or merging modules or chapters" covers the splitting and merging clause.
- "moving or renaming a requirement" covers the requirement-rename clause.
- "so that evidence whose content is unchanged is not invalidated" covers the purpose clause.

The actual description in `assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md` contains all four phrases. A description that dropped any of these clauses would fail the test.

Bundling is also covered. The `SKILLS` constant and `skill_files` list `habeas-refactor` among the bundled skills. `bundled_skill_descriptions_say_when_to_use_them` also checks the `habeas-refactor` description opening.

I found no untested obligation and no ambiguity in the requirement.
